# Results at a glance {#results-at-a-glance}

[New in the 2026 web edition: a scoring summary of the report's 2012 totals. This is a condensed version of the recommendations in [Section 5.3](#which-tool-should-i-get-summary-of-recommendations).]{.edition-label}

::: {.glance}

::: {.glance-row .top}
[1]{.rank} [articy:draft]{.tool} [464]{.score}

The strongest tool for managing a branching story end to end, but the most expensive. In 2012, conversation simulation and script export were still on its roadmap.
:::

::: {.glance-row}
[2]{.rank} [Chat Mapper]{.tool} [401]{.score}

Easy to learn, free for personal use, and has a conversation simulator, but it needs some Lua scripting and can't manage multiple narrative paths.
:::

::: {.glance-row}
[3]{.rank} [DA Toolset]{.tool} [333]{.score}

Lets you build and play a working game, at the cost of a very high learning curve and subpar documentation.
:::

::: {.glance-row}
[4]{.rank} [Excel]{.tool} [330]{.score}

Cheap, familiar, and flexible, but every cross-reference, condition, and name change has to be updated by hand.
:::

:::
